newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey government to curb Islamists - NSC.
newsitem.headline: Turkey government to curb Islamists - NSC.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government has promised to go ahead with measures aimed at curbing religious activism, according to a statement issued after a crisis meeting of the country's political and army leaders.
"Agreement was reached that the cabinet will work on the co-ordinating, budgeting, planning and programming phases... of the decision," the National Security Council said.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist head of government since the Ottoman Empire collapsed at the end of World War One, promised the crackdown two months ago.
But stalling since then by his Islam-based Welfare Party has upset his conservative True Path Party coalition partners and angered military leaders, the defenders of the modern, secularist tradition.
Two True Path ministers resigned earlier on Saturday because of Erbakan's reluctance to clamp down on his Islamist supporters.

Top of the generals' list of 18 anti-Islamist demands is a call for educational reform that would require students to attend eight years of secular schooling -- rather than the current five years -- before optional Koranic training.
The army has ousted three governments since 1960 but is reluctant to stage another coup for fear of damaging Turkey's relations with the West.
